title: WPMS/1336/2013 of Ajit Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1336 of 2013 (M/S)
Ajit Singh. ........Petitioner
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others. .......Respondents
Mr. Siddhartha Singh, Advocate with Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate present for
the petitioner.
Mr. Paresh Tripathi, Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand/respondent Nos. 1 to 4.
Mr. Rajesh Sharma, Advocate present for the respondent No. 5.
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. G.D. Joshi, Advocate
present for the respondent No.7.
Mr. Yogesh Pandey, Advocate present for respondent Nos. 8 to 12.
Dated: July 2, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
2. Present writ petition has been filed by the petitioner
for following reliefs:-
"I. Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the letter dated
21st May, 2013 issued by the Joint Secretary to
the Government, decision dated 22.05.2013
taken by the Uttarakhand Cooperative
Resham Federation Ltd., order dated 27th
May, 2013 issued by the Secretary Cooperative
& decision dated 13.04.2013, whereby the
representatives of all these five societies were
elected for federation.
II. Issue any suitable writ, order or direction,
which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and
proper on the basis of the facts and
circumstances of the case.
III. Award the cost of the petition to the
petitioner."
3. Preliminary objection has been raised by the
counsel for the respondents that the writ petition filed by

2
the petitioner is not maintainable, as the petitioner has no
locus to file the writ petition. Since, election to the Apex
body i.e. the Uttarakhand State Co-operative Federation
Limited (hereinafter referred to as the Federation) is to be
done by delegates of primary cooperative societies, the
writ petition could only be filed by the cooperative society
and not the petitioner who is simply a delegate of one of
the said cooperative societies. In support of their
arguments, the learned counsel for the respondents relied
upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, reported in
(2001) 4 Supreme Court Cases-734 'Vinoy Kumar vs.
State of U.P. and others' and the judgment of the Division
Bench of the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court, reported in
2005 (4) AWC 3563 'Smt. Kesari Devi vs. State of U.P.
and others'. In the said judgment, the Hon'ble Court
referring the judgment M.S. Jayaraj case, has observed
that Court must examine the locus from all angles. The
Hon'ble Court further observed that a person aggrieved
means a person, who is injured or is adversely affected in
a legal sense.
4. On the question of maintainability of the petition,
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that since the
petitioner was elected as a Member of Resham Kitpalan
Cooperative Society, Chakkitola, Niranjanpur, Dehradun
and he has right to caste the vote and elect the chairman,
vice chairman, members of committee of Management
and office bearers of the Federation, he has every right to
file writ petition. He submitted that by means of this
petition, the petitioner has tried to challenge the election
of delegates who were illegally elected. He further
submitted that by illegal inclusion of private respondents
and their delegates in Federation, the election of

3
Committee of Management of the Federation would be
effected.
5. On merit, the learned counsel for the petitioner
argued that induction of the private respondent nos. 8 to
12 in Federation, was not done by Administrator himself
but the same was done by him on the instruction of the
Joint Secretary of the State Government. He submitted
that such induction is under compulsion and is not legal.
The second argument of the petitioner is that Rule 433 of
Uttarakhand Cooperative Societies Rules (in short "the
Rules") provides that any person, who has been enrolled
as a member 45 days before the date of election, shall only
be included in the list of voters. He submitted that in the
present case, the election of the delegates of primary
society was held on 13.04.2013. The private respondents
were included as member of Federation on 22.05.2013.
Therefore, the election of the delegates of the societies is
in violation of Rule 433 of the Rules. He further submitted
that in any case, election of the delegates of primary
society cannot be held prior to induction of the society as
member of Federation. He also referred the counter
affidavit of respondent nos. 8 to 12 in which it is stated
that the election of the delegates of these Societies was
held in anticipation of membership of Federation. On the
basis of these arguments, the learned counsel for the
petitioner argued that since the induction of the
respondent nos. 8 to 12, as member of Federation, is
illegal and same was granted under the dictate of the
Secretary of the State Government, the writ petition
deserves to be allowed.

4
6. In reply, the learned counsel for the respondents
also referred the letter written by Joint Secretary dated
21.05.2013 and submitted that by reading this letter dated
21.05.2013 it is absolutely clear that there is no direction
to Managing Director of the Federation to include the
private respondents as members. The letter only says that
membership of the Federation can be granted to the
Societies.
7. Learned counsel for the respondents further
submitted that, in fact, on 08.1.2013, the respondent
societies were registered and election of delegates of the
societies was held on 13.04.2013. Thus, this election of
delegate was held after a period of 45 days from the date
of registration of the societies. He further submitted that
on 22.05.2013, societies were inducted as members of the
Federation and date of election of members of Committee
of Management, including office bearers, is scheduled on
12th & 13th July, 2013. The election date is after 45 days of
grant of membership. It is also submitted that rule and
byelaws do not bar the election of delegates in
anticipation of membership of the Federation.
8. Learned counsel for the respondents relied upon
Rule 457-b (2) and (3) of the Rules and submitted that
since the election of the Committee of Management of
primary societies and their delegates was held on
13.04.2013, consequently, petitioner cannot challenge the
election of the delegates of the societies of the private
respondents in the writ petition. The petition, challenging
the election dated 13.04.2013 cannot be entertained. The
election dated 13.04.2013 can only be challenged under
Rule 457 of the Act.

5
9. In rejoinder, the learned counsel for the petitioner
submits that Rule 457 of the Rules will not apply in the
present case, as the delegates of the respondent nos. 8 to
12 have been elected to caste their votes in violation of the
Rules.
10. I have considered the submissions of learned
counsel for the parties.
11. As far as locus-standi of the petitioner to file writ
petition is concerned, I find that petitioner is member of
Resham Kitpalan Co-operative Society, Chakkitola and an
elected delegate of this society for the Federation. He has
a role to play in the election of members of Committee of
Management, including office bearers of the Federation.
But this right is as a delegate of the society, which is the
member of the Federation. The society, of which the
petitioner is a delegate, has not come before the Court,
which alone could have a locus to challenge the induction
of the other societies. Thus, it is held that the petitioner
has no locus to file the present writ petition.
12. Even otherwise, the election can be challenged on
the grounds mentioned in Rule 457 of the Rules. Rule 457
of the Rule is being reproduced hereinafter:-
Rule 457 of the Uttaranchal Co-operative
Societies Rules, 2004: "(1) The election in a
co-operative society shall not be called in
question either by arbitration or otherwise
except on the ground that-
 (a) the election has not been a fair election by
reasons that corrupt practice, bribery or
undue influence has extensively prevailed at
the election, or
 (b) the result of the election has been
materially affected-

6
 (i) by improper acceptance or rejection of any
nomination, or
 (ii) by improper reception, refusal or rejection
of voters, or
(iii) by gross failure to comply with the
provisions of the Act, the Rules or the Byelaws
of the Society.
Explanation- For the purpose of this rule
corruption, bribery or undue influence shall
have the meaning assigned to each under
Section 123 of the Representation of People
Act, 1951.
(2) A dispute relating to election shall be
referred by the aggrieved party within 45 days
of the declaration of the result.
13. Rule 457 (1) (b) (ii) provides that the election in a
Co-operative Society can be questioned if the result of the
election has been materially affected by improper
reception, refusal or rejection of voters. Rule 457 (1) (b)
(iii) provides that a dispute relating to the result of the
election can also be challenged where the result of the
election has been materially affected by gross failure to
comply with the provisions of the Act, the Rules or the
Byelaws of the Society.
14. In the case in hand, it is admitted between the
parties that the election of the Committee of Management
and members and of delegates for other societies was held
on 12 and 13th April, 2013 and the election of the
Committed of Management and the office bearers of the
Federation is also notified and is scheduled to be held on
12.07.2013 and 13.07.2013.
15. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Shri
Sant Sadguru Janardan Swami (Moingiri Maharaj)
Sahakari Dugdha Utpadak Sanstha and another Vs. State
of Maharastra and others reported in 2001 (8) S.C.C. 509,
has held that once election process having been set in

7
motion, the High Court should not stay the continuation
of the election process even though there may be some
alleged illegality or breach or rules while preparing the
electoral roll. Paragraph no.12 of the judgment is
reproduced below:-
"12. In view of our finding that preparation of
the electoral roll being an intermediate stage
in the process of election of the Managing
Committee of a specified society and the
election process having been set in motion, it
is well settled that the High Court should not
stay the continuation of the election process
even though there may be some alleged
illegality or breach of rules while preparing
the electoral roll. It is not disputed that the
election in question has already been held and
the result thereof has been stayed by an order
of this Court, and once the result of the
election is declared, it would be open to the
appellants to challenge the election of the
returned candidate, if aggrieved, by means of
an election petition before the Election
Tribunal."
16. In view of the aforesaid discussion, the writ petition
is dismissed.
17. Interim order stands vacated accordingly.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 02.07.2013
JKJ/NCM:
